name: DCA-A4-01 · Download Problem Self-Service (reissue access without a human)

parameters.content:
## 🔁 Download Problem Self-Service
**"I can't get my file" → verified → fresh link sent. No human.**

### Setup (about 12 minutes)
1. **⚙️ Config** → `storeName`, `fromEmail`, `downloadBaseUrl`.
2. **🔑 Sign the new link** → use the **same secret** as A1-01 and A1-02.
3. Seed `knownOrders` from your order log, **or** wire the lookup node to
   your real order source (see the note in **🔎 Verify entitlement**).
4. Attach SMTP. Activate.
5. Put the form URL in your delivery emails: *"Trouble downloading?"*

### Why this one is worth building first
It is not a wide variety of problems. It is **one problem** wearing
different clothes — and it dominates a digital seller's inbox.

### 🤖 Why no AI here
B1-01 answers *questions* — that needs judgement, and sometimes a model.

This performs a **transaction**: verify entitlement, reissue access.

No model means no API cost, no latency, and **no possibility of inventing
a policy**. Routing this through an LLM would be slower, more expensive
and less safe.

Use the right tool. Not everything needs an agent.

### 🔐 This is an access-granting endpoint
Automatic reissue can be abused — anyone who learns a customer's email
could request their file.

**Three deliberate controls:**
1. The link is sent **only** to the email on the original order — never
   to a reply-to address supplied in the request.
2. Requests are rate-limited per email per day.
3. Anything over the limit **escalates to you**, it does not silently
   refuse.

⚠️ Point 3 matters: a control that fails closed and says nothing just
creates the support ticket this template exists to prevent.

### 📊 What it deflects
| Case | Handled |
| --- | --- |
| Link expired | ✅ auto |
| Download cap reached | ✅ auto |
| Lost the email | ✅ auto |
| Wrong email on order | 🙋 escalates |
| No order found | 🙋 escalates |
| Over rate limit | 🙋 escalates |

The first three are most of the volume.

nodes.name: 🆘 Download help request
nodes.notes: POST {email, orderId?}. Link this form from your delivery emails.

nodes.name: ⚙️ Config
nodes.notes: knownOrders maps email → {orderId, productId}. Seed it, or wire the verify node to your real order store.

nodes.name: 🛡️ Guard · validate + dedupe
nodes.notes: Validates required fields and drops duplicate deliveries. Safe to re-run.

nodes.name: 🔎 Verify entitlement
nodes.notes: Entitlement + rate limit. Replace the lookup with your real order store; keep the return shape.

nodes.name: 🔑 Sign the new link
nodes.notes: ⚠️ Must be the SAME secret used in A1-01 and A1-02, or the link will not verify.

nodes.name: 🔗 Build the fresh link
nodes.notes: Same URL contract as A1-01 — verified by a cross-template test.

nodes.name: 📧 Send the fresh link

parameters.subject: ={{ 'Your download link — ' + $json.__config.storeName }}
parameters.html:
={{ '
' + '

Here is your download

' + '

No problem — here is a fresh link for order ' + $json.orderId + '.

' + 'Download now' + '

Valid until ' + $json.expiresHuman + ', up to ' + $json.__config.maxDownloads + ' downloads.

' + '

Still stuck? Reply to this email and a person will help.

' + '

nodes.notes: Sent to the address on the ORDER, not one supplied in the request.

nodes.name: 🙋 Escalate to a human
nodes.notes: Explains what happened and what it usually means — not just a bare handoff.

nodes.name: 📨 Tell the human
nodes.notes: Swap for Slack/Telegram if you prefer.

nodes.name: 📒 Deflection log
nodes.notes: Track the auto-resolved vs escalated ratio. That ratio is the template's value.

nodes.name: 🚨 Handle failure
nodes.notes: Structured failure record. Wire to your alert channel.

nodes.name: ↩️ Confirm to the buyer

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, message: "If that email has an order with us, a fresh download link is on its way." }) }}

nodes.notes: Answer fast so the provider does not retry on timeout.
